cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Bright Scarf Slow Track
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.ageModifications: Infant 0–6 months (younger: look only; older: may bat scarf)
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Support slow visual tracking with a bright moving scarf.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: Baby watches a large bright scarf move slowly across their view while you name the color in a calm voice.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.preparation:
Choose one high-contrast bright color
Clear visual clutter behind you
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.setup: Place baby comfortably on back or supported side on a mat.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Settle baby and gain eye contact first
2. Hold scarf about 8–12 inches away
3. Move slowly left, pause, then right
4. Name the color once or twice
5. Stop when baby looks away
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.teacherLanguage: Look… see the bright red? Watching… watching.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.observationOpportunities: Tracks scarf briefly; stays calm while looking.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.safetyNotes: Keep scarf away from face/neck; never leave draped on baby.
teacherTips: Slower than you think — pause when eyes lock on.
observationPrompts: Tracks scarf briefly; stays calm while looking.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.imageBriefSetup: Caregiver kneeling on mat holding one bright scarf 8–12 inches from infant on back.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Colorful Tummy Time Look
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.ageModifications: Infant 0–6 months (use chest-to-chest for very young infants)
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Encourage head lifting during awake tummy time with a colorful visual anchor.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: During supervised tummy time, a bright toy or cloth sits in view to invite looking and brief head lifts.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.materials:
Tummy-time mat
1 large bright toy or cloth
Optional support roll
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.preparation:
Place colorful item at eye level in front of baby
Set timer mindset for short bursts
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.setup: Awake baby on tummy on firm mat; colorful item in front.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Place baby on tummy when alert
2. Set bright item in easy view
3. Get face-to-face beside baby and talk
4. Celebrate any head lift or looking
5. Return to back for rest as needed
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.teacherLanguage: You are looking! Bright yellow is right here.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.observationOpportunities: Lifts head briefly; looks toward colorful item.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.safetyNotes: Tummy time only when awake and supervised. Back to sleep.
teacherTips: Chest-to-chest counts as tummy time for newborns.
observationPrompts: Lifts head briefly; looks toward colorful item.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.imageBriefSetup: Infant on tummy on mat with one large bright toy at eye level; caregiver face nearby.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Face-to-Face Color Talk
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Connect caregiver face (best early visual target) with a simple color prop.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: You hold baby close, smile, and slowly show one bright cloth while talking. Faces stay the main focus.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.preparation: Sit where light falls on your face, not in baby’s eyes
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.setup: Hold baby 8–12 inches from your face with cloth nearby.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Gain eye contact and smile
2. Show cloth beside your face briefly
3. Name the color in a soft voice
4. Hide cloth and return to face play
5. End with a cuddle
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.teacherLanguage: Hi! I see you. Here is soft blue.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.observationOpportunities: Looks at face; glances toward cloth.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.safetyNotes: Support head/neck; stop if baby turns away.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.cleanupTips: Set cloth aside for wash if mouthed.
teacherTips: Face first, prop second — never replace interaction with objects.
observationPrompts: Looks at face; glances toward cloth.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: One-Color Slow Track
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Practice tracking with a single bold color to reduce visual overload.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: Baby watches one solid-color scarf move slowly while you pause for focus.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.materials:
One solid bright scarf
Mat
Support pillow if needed
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.preparation: Remove other bright toys from view
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.setup: Baby on back or side; one scarf only.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Show still scarf first
2. Move slowly side to side
3. Pause when baby fixates
4. Name color once
5. Rest
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.safetyNotes: Arm’s reach; no scarf near neck.
teacherTips: One color beats a rainbow pile for young infants.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Color Lap Bounce Song
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Pair gentle rhythm and voice with a simple color prop.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: Baby is held securely while you hum/sing and show a soft colored cloth with tiny bounces.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.materials:
Soft colored cloth
Chair
Your voice
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.preparation: Choose a calm short song phrase
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.setup: Sit with baby well supported in arms.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Settle baby in arms
2. Show cloth
3. Sing a short color phrase
4. Add tiny responsive bounces
5. Stillness and smile to close
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.teacherLanguage: Bounce, bounce — soft yellow with you.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.observationOpportunities: Settles to voice; glances at cloth.
teacherTips: Match bounce to baby’s state — calm babies need almost no bounce.
observationPrompts: Settles to voice; glances at cloth.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Color Board Book Together
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Share a brief board-book look with face-to-face connection.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: You hold a color board book where baby can see pages and your face, staying on 1–2 pages.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.materials:
Color board book
Lap or mat
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.setup: Lap hold or tummy-to-tummy with book angled toward baby.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Show cover briefly
2. Open to one bright page
3. Point near the color shape
4. Name color slowly
5. Close with smile
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.teacherLanguage: This page is bright green. Looking together.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.observationOpportunities: Looks at page; looks back at caregiver.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.safetyNotes: Board books only; no paper tears near mouth unsupervised.
teacherTips: Stopping early is success.
observationPrompts: Looks at page; looks back at caregiver.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Soft Color Reach
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.ageModifications: Best for ~3–6 months; younger infants may only look
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Invite reaching toward a large soft colorful toy when ready.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: A large yellow (or bright) rattle sits just within reach during supervised floor time. Younger babies may only look.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.preparation: Check toy is mouth-safe and too large to choke
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.setup: Baby on back; toy held or propped within swipe range.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Gain attention on toy
2. Hold steady within reach
3. Allow bat/reach attempts
4. Celebrate any contact
5. Offer grasp help only if baby is ready
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.teacherLanguage: Can you reach the bright rattle?
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.observationOpportunities: Bats or reaches; brings hands toward midline.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.safetyNotes: No small parts; sanitize after mouthing.
teacherTips: If no reach yet, keep as a looking toy — still valuable.
observationPrompts: Bats or reaches; brings hands toward midline.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.imageBriefSetup: Infant on back reaching toward large yellow rattle held by caregiver.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Tummy Color Mirror Look
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Combine tummy time with mirror looking and a color accent.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: Baby does short tummy time facing a baby-safe mirror with one colorful cloth beside it.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.preparation: Angle mirror for baby’s face view
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.setup: Mirror at edge of mat; cloth to the side — not covering mirror.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Place baby on tummy
2. Point to baby’s face in mirror
3. Show cloth briefly beside mirror
4. Talk about looking
5. Rest on back
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.teacherLanguage: I see you! And soft blue beside you.
teacherTips: Your face beside the mirror beats any toy.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.imageBriefSetup: Tummy-time mat with baby-safe mirror and one bright cloth at side.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Color Cloth Touch Basket
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Explore soft colorful cloths with eyes and hands under supervision.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: A shallow basket holds 2–3 large soft colored cloths. Baby looks and may touch while you narrate.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.preparation:
Use only oversized cloths
Limit to 2–3 colors
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.setup: Basket near baby on mat; you seated close.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Show one cloth from basket
2. Drape lightly on your hand for baby to see/touch
3. Name color and texture
4. Offer second cloth if interested
5. Put cloths away before baby tires
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.safetyNotes: Never cover baby’s face; prevent bundling/entanglement.
teacherTips: Less is more — two cloths often beat five.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.imageBriefSetup: Shallow basket with 2–3 bright cloths beside infant on mat.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Soft Color Texture Mitts
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Offer safe textured color mitts for looking and gentle touch.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: You wear or hold a soft textured mitt in a bright color and invite baby to look and pat.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.materials:
Washable textured mitt or cloth square with sewn texture
Mat
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.setup: Sit facing baby with mitt on your hand.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Show mitt still
2. Move slowly into view
3. Allow touch on mitt (not face covering)
4. Name color and feel (soft/bumpy)
5. Remove if overstimulating
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.safetyNotes: Secure all parts; sanitize; no detachable decorations.
teacherTips: Your paced presentation matters more than the mitt design.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.imageBriefSetup: Caregiver hand with bright textured mitt near infant’s hands.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Color Hello with Caregiver
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Use a short greeting song with a color prop to support social connection.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: Each baby gets a personal hello while you show a color cloth and sing a brief greeting.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.setup: Hold or sit with one baby at a time.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Make eye contact
2. Show cloth
3. Sing hello with color word
4. Pause for baby response
5. Kiss or cuddle close
teacherTips: One baby at a time beats a group performance.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Soft Color Sway Hold
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Provide gentle vestibular movement while baby looks at a color scarf.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: Holding baby securely, you sway side to side while a green scarf stays in view.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.setup: Stand or sit with baby held upright/supported.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Hold baby securely
2. Show scarf in view
3. Sway slowly left/right
4. Name color softly
5. Stillness to finish
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.observationOpportunities: Calms or alerts to movement; looks at scarf.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.safetyNotes: Two-hand secure hold; no spinning or dipping.
teacherTips: Match sway to breathing; stop if baby startles.
observationPrompts: Calms or alerts to movement; looks at scarf.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Color Song Cuddle
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Close the week with a calm color song and cuddle.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: Babies are held or sit supported while you sing the original Look at the Bright Color song with one cloth.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Settle in cuddle
2. Show cloth
3. Sing short original song
4. Pause for coos
5. Quiet hold
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.teacherLanguage: Look, look, see the bright color.
teacherTips: Repetition across the week builds familiarity.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Favorite Color Page Replay
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Replay a page babies noticed earlier in the week.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: Return to one favorite bright board-book page and enjoy a short second look.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Open to favorite page
2. Point and name color
3. Wait for looking
4. Turn away and back once (simple peek)
5. Close warmly
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.teacherLanguage: This was our favorite bright page!
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.observationOpportunities: Shows recognition interest; stays engaged briefly.
teacherTips: Preference is data — reuse what worked.
observationPrompts: Shows recognition interest; stays engaged briefly.

cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.title: Shaded Color Stroll
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.objective: Notice real-world colors outdoors with caregiver pointing and talk.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.description: In shade, you stroll or sit outdoors and point to large colorful things (flowers, balls, clothing) while narrating.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.materials:
Stroller or outdoor blanket
Sun protection as needed
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.steps:
1. Settle baby facing out or toward you
2. Point to one colorful object
3. Name color and object
4. Pause for looking
5. Return indoors before overstimulation/heat
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.teacherLanguage: See the yellow flower? Bright outside.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.observationOpportunities: Looks toward pointed object; stays content outdoors.
cur-lp-infant-colors-all-around-us:item-.safetyNotes: Shade, hydration for adults, never leave stroller unattended; follow safe sleep if nap begins.
teacherTips: One or two pointed objects beat a tour.
observationPrompts: Looks toward pointed object; stays content outdoors.

week.weeklyOverview: This week focuses on looking, tracking, reaching, and warm caregiver talk with bright colors — not naming drills or crafts. Younger infants mostly look and listen; older infants may reach and grasp when ready.
week.objectives:
Support visual attention and slow tracking with bright, simple materials
Offer supervised tummy-time looking with colorful anchors
Encourage reaching/grasping only when developmentally ready
Build connection through face-to-face talk and short songs
Share brief, visually clear board-book moments
week.weeklyMaterials:
Large bright scarves (chiffon or soft fabric)
Soft colored cloth squares (too large to choke)
Baby-safe mirror
Large soft colored rattles/balls
Tummy-time mat
Simple color board books
Support pillow/roll for positioning
week.familyConnection: Invite families to name one bright color during a diaper change or walk — keep it playful, not a quiz.
week.adaptations: Younger infants: closer, slower, shorter. Older infants: offer graspable large toys. Reduce stimulation if baby looks away.
week.vocabularyWords:
look
see
bright
red
blue
yellow
green
soft
reach
watch
week.teacherPreparation:
Sanitize cloths/rattles and set a calm floor space
Choose 2–3 bright colors for the day (avoid clutter)
Plan short bursts (1–5 minutes) between care routines

monday.materials:

Large soft colored rattles/balls
Tummy-time mat

monday.safetyNotes: Stay within arm’s reach. No small parts, cords, or bags. Back to sleep; tummy time only when awake and supervised.

items.title: Tummy Color Mirror Look
items.objective: Combine tummy time with mirror looking and a color accent.
items.description: Baby does short tummy time facing a baby-safe mirror with one colorful cloth beside it.
items.preparation: Angle mirror for baby’s face view
items.setup: Mirror at edge of mat; cloth to the side — not covering mirror.
items.steps:
1. Place baby on tummy
2. Point to baby’s face in mirror
3. Show cloth briefly beside mirror
4. Talk about looking
5. Rest on back
items.teacherLanguage: I see you! And soft blue beside you.
teacherTips: Your face beside the mirror beats any toy.
items.imageBriefSetup: Tummy-time mat with baby-safe mirror and one bright cloth at side.

items.title: Color Cloth Touch Basket
items.objective: Explore soft colorful cloths with eyes and hands under supervision.
items.description: A shallow basket holds 2–3 large soft colored cloths. Baby looks and may touch while you narrate.
items.preparation:
Use only oversized cloths
Limit to 2–3 colors
items.setup: Basket near baby on mat; you seated close.
items.steps:
1. Show one cloth from basket
2. Drape lightly on your hand for baby to see/touch
3. Name color and texture
4. Offer second cloth if interested
5. Put cloths away before baby tires
items.safetyNotes: Never cover baby’s face; prevent bundling/entanglement.
teacherTips: Less is more — two cloths often beat five.
items.imageBriefSetup: Shallow basket with 2–3 bright cloths beside infant on mat.

thursday.objectives:
Explore soft color textures
Practice greeting with color prop
Sway with color cloth
thursday.materials:
Large bright scarves (chiffon or soft fabric)
Soft colored cloth squares (too large to choke)
Baby-safe mirror
Large soft colored rattles/balls
Tummy-time mat
Simple color board books
Support pillow/roll for positioning
thursday.vocabulary:
look
see
bright
red
blue
yellow
green
soft
reach
watch
thursday.outdoorPlay: Quiet outdoor sway with scarf if weather allows.
thursday.adaptations: Younger infants: closer, slower, shorter. Older infants: offer graspable large toys. Reduce stimulation if baby looks away.
thursday.safetyNotes: Stay within arm’s reach. No small parts, cords, or bags. Back to sleep; tummy time only when awake and supervised.

items.title: Soft Color Texture Mitts
items.objective: Offer safe textured color mitts for looking and gentle touch.
items.description: You wear or hold a soft textured mitt in a bright color and invite baby to look and pat.
items.materials:
Washable textured mitt or cloth square with sewn texture
Mat
items.setup: Sit facing baby with mitt on your hand.
items.steps:
1. Show mitt still
2. Move slowly into view
3. Allow touch on mitt (not face covering)
4. Name color and feel (soft/bumpy)
5. Remove if overstimulating
items.safetyNotes: Secure all parts; sanitize; no detachable decorations.
teacherTips: Your paced presentation matters more than the mitt design.
items.imageBriefSetup: Caregiver hand with bright textured mitt near infant’s hands.

items.title: Color Hello with Caregiver
items.objective: Use a short greeting song with a color prop to support social connection.
items.description: Each baby gets a personal hello while you show a color cloth and sing a brief greeting.
items.setup: Hold or sit with one baby at a time.
items.steps:
1. Make eye contact
2. Show cloth
3. Sing hello with color word
4. Pause for baby response
5. Kiss or cuddle close
teacherTips: One baby at a time beats a group performance.

items.title: Soft Color Sway Hold
items.objective: Provide gentle vestibular movement while baby looks at a color scarf.
items.description: Holding baby securely, you sway side to side while a green scarf stays in view.
items.setup: Stand or sit with baby held upright/supported.
items.steps:
1. Hold baby securely
2. Show scarf in view
3. Sway slowly left/right
4. Name color softly
5. Stillness to finish
items.observationOpportunities: Calms or alerts to movement; looks at scarf.
items.safetyNotes: Two-hand secure hold; no spinning or dipping.
teacherTips: Match sway to breathing; stop if baby startles.

friday.objectives:
Review through song
Replay a favorite page
Notice outdoor colors safely
friday.materials:
Large bright scarves (chiffon or soft fabric)
Soft colored cloth squares (too large to choke)
Baby-safe mirror
Large soft colored rattles/balls
Tummy-time mat
Simple color board books
Support pillow/roll for positioning
friday.vocabulary:
look
see
bright
red
blue
yellow
green
soft
reach
watch
friday.outdoorPlay: Shaded color stroll — point to flowers, signs, or clothing colors.
friday.adaptations: Younger infants: closer, slower, shorter. Older infants: offer graspable large toys. Reduce stimulation if baby looks away.
friday.safetyNotes: Stay within arm’s reach. No small parts, cords, or bags. Back to sleep; tummy time only when awake and supervised.

items.title: Color Song Cuddle
items.objective: Close the week with a calm color song and cuddle.
items.description: Babies are held or sit supported while you sing the original Look at the Bright Color song with one cloth.
items.steps:
1. Settle in cuddle
2. Show cloth
3. Sing short original song
4. Pause for coos
5. Quiet hold
items.teacherLanguage: Look, look, see the bright color.
teacherTips: Repetition across the week builds familiarity.

items.title: Favorite Color Page Replay
items.objective: Replay a page babies noticed earlier in the week.
items.description: Return to one favorite bright board-book page and enjoy a short second look.
items.steps:
1. Open to favorite page
2. Point and name color
3. Wait for looking
4. Turn away and back once (simple peek)
5. Close warmly
items.teacherLanguage: This was our favorite bright page!
items.observationOpportunities: Shows recognition interest; stays engaged briefly.
teacherTips: Preference is data — reuse what worked.

items.title: Shaded Color Stroll
items.objective: Notice real-world colors outdoors with caregiver pointing and talk.
items.description: In shade, you stroll or sit outdoors and point to large colorful things (flowers, balls, clothing) while narrating.
items.materials:
Stroller or outdoor blanket
Sun protection as needed
items.steps:
1. Settle baby facing out or toward you
2. Point to one colorful object
3. Name color and object
4. Pause for looking
5. Return indoors before overstimulation/heat
items.teacherLanguage: See the yellow flower? Bright outside.
items.observationOpportunities: Looks toward pointed object; stays content outdoors.
items.safetyNotes: Shade, hydration for adults, never leave stroller unattended; follow safe sleep if nap begins.
teacherTips: One or two pointed objects beat a tour.

songs.lyrics:
Look, look, see the bright color.
Look, look, watching with me.
Soft and slow, we smile and say the color name.
songs.motions: Show cloth; gentle sway; smile at infant.

songs.title: Twinkle Twinkle Little Star
songs.notes: Public-domain melody; use as calm cuddle song with a yellow cloth.

songs.title: Color Hello Song (LLH original)
songs.lyrics:
Hello red, hello blue,
I see bright colors with you.
Hello yellow, hello green,
Smiling faces in between.
songs.motions: Show one cloth per color line.

Have board book ready with one bookmark page
observationFocus: Any reaching when offered within range?
Cues for overstimulation (looking away, arching, fussing)?
